statements.text: If the Chinese attack us with an AI [artificial intelligence]-enabled force, an autonomous weapon system of some sort, and we meet that with an American manned alternative, who do you expect to win?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on Indo-Pacific national security challenges, featuring an exchange between Representative Seth Moulton and Admiral John Aquilino.

statements.text: And, therefore, their AI won't as well. I am confident that their AI is being trained to do heinous things or at the very least pay little regard for civilian casualties and collateral damage, which will almost certainly make their AI more deadly and effective. [...] So in an AI versus AI battle, they will have a massive advantage because they won't constrain their weapons in the ethical ways we do. So the point that I am making is that we have to do work on developing an international agreement to codify these standards, so it is not just us who are following them, and then we at least have some hope of ensuring our adversaries' worst instincts are at least to some degree constrained.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on DOD IT, digital developments, and AI for FY2023.

statements.text: you mentioned that when you bring forward new AI capabilities you have to ensure their employment meets our ethical norms and standards. This is, of course, exactly what we would expect. But do you believe that our adversaries adhere to the same ethical standards?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on DOD IT, digital developments, and AI for FY2023.

statements.text: If there are no rules for the use of AI, we are going to still constrain ourselves by our values but our adversaries may not, which gives them an inherent advantage.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on the future of warfare and Pentagon readiness.

statements.text: We haven't even discussed arms control when it comes to AI. Mr. Brose, perhaps I will start with you.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on the future of war and Pentagon preparedness.

statements.text: Gentlemen, I am concerned that we are losing in key areas of the strategic competition with the CCP. I would prefer that we win.
statements.context: Opening statement at a House Armed Services CITI Subcommittee hearing on AI and defense, March 9, 2023.

statements.text: I think this is a great opportunity for the Marine Corps to continue to lead. [...] Would you be willing to get us a report by this September for what the Marine Corps is doing today to integrate AI and what you can do to accelerate that, to give that advantage to our Marines and warfighters in the near future?
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on the FY 2024 National Defense Authorization Act, during an exchange between Rep. Seth Moulton and the Commandant of the Marine Corps.

statements.text: Dr. Eric Schmidt stated that it would be a "'Dr. Strangelove' scenario" to let China set the rules of the road for AI weapons. I worry that AI weapons could become even more dangerous than nuclear weapons, because there's been no international effort whatsoever to rein them in. I'm not afraid of how we will use them; I'm afraid of how our adversaries might use them.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on U.S. leadership in critical and emerging technologies.

statements.text: because of civil-military fusion in China, China is doing this today, right? I mean, they have their top AI companies working on their military problems. So this is another thing where we have to have the urgency to get this done.
statements.context: Remarks by Rep. Seth Moulton during a House Armed Services Committee hearing on AI and DOD operations.

statements.text: If America falls short in this new AI arms race, someone else will set the moral guardrails for its use, and once that happens, it will be very difficult to pull back," that "The lack of agreed-upon guardrails and accountability surrounding autonomous weaponry is precisely why it could end up being the most dangerous weapon we have ever seen.
statements.context: Rep. Moulton speaks at a hearing titled 'Algorithms and Authoritarians: Why U.S. AI Must Lead,' pressing witnesses on the need for international AI norms.
